This is a fascinating research at the intersections of the inner workings of Human memory and Information processing; What do we know, based on the Sciences and Math (Gestalt, Prototype Theory, Category Theory, Neuroscience, etc.) as to why we as Human beings struggle with certain kinds of information memory tasks (such as memorizing numerical or non-specific addresses, e.g., "1.305.239.2") even if they afford a more optimal and efficient means of storing, memorizing and retrieving information?

"apple" is somehow interpreted as a tangible object (perhaps in imagination or working memory... though research here is inconclusive.). It has prototype properties and features, typically red or green, usually average size. It's material properties are somewhat naturally glossy, and it's flavor is sweet and refreshing.

However, "3/5/203e29" could represent the same thing, and perhaps an even more effective form of information transfer. However, this is where we enter something I can call, Entropy Episteme space

One can memorize "a huge long string of unique data" yet struggle to dinstinguish between "3501" and "3051" ... it may be more than mere pattern recognition... and given what we know about the Language Centres of the Brain; Language is not merely a social artifact, it is an Ancient tool of Communication; a form of communication spanning far to the beginnings of life (various animals have been empirically shown to speak in their own languages.)

Given the social-neuroscience circuitry, one may understand that Language is not essentially an optimal or efficient strategy, if we are merely studying the scope of information-storage-efficiency. However, storing information, that is required by context, of an undefined mass, of a dynamic, often unpredictable enviornment, is itself a different architecture... and in some sense, the mess itself will be necessary (Ashby's Requisite Variety and Neuroscience "Noise Floor" is supporting material here.)

Still, one may wonder "why not memorize numbers or addresses, or effective methods of memory, given the already limited bandwidth of information management today? One that is becoming increasingly pressurized by the currents of algorithms and the unmanageable depths of cyber information spaces."

Memorizing "3013e3" rather than "life/finances/account/e3" introduces a fascinating direction for Human-memory-algorithm... which is perhaps the natural direction of this study.

The fact that we can memorize massive vocabulary (and retain a large mass, even if pruned or unused for extended periods of time...) but we struggle with even the most basic of abstract concepts (as previously mentioned...) most likely reveals a fundamental inner workings of how we memorize such an enormous vocabulary, yet struggle memorizing the periodic table, or classical mathematics multiplication table.

Applications & Implications in the real world: undefined.
